goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:52 — only the *host* of embed_url is validated, so an unauthenticated request with a forged Referer makes the server fetch and auto-publish any path/query on the blog (search-result and 404 pages that echo attacker text) as a raw_html post, and the attacker-chosen URL is interpolated unescaped into `href='#{url}'` at topic_embed.rb:13 (e.g. `http://blog/x'/onmouseover=alert(1)//`, which survives Nokogiri re-serialization in absolutize_urls) — unauthenticated stored XSS plus topic spam

lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` is run inline and unrescued, so any exception from the feed (network error, malformed XML, one bad item) propagates and prevents the `fetch_http` fallback on line 45 from ever running — one broken feed disables direct retrieval for every embedded URL

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, and there is no `rescue` around it. In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then processes items; `open` (network/HTTP errors), parsing, or item processing can raise exceptions. Any such exception would bubble up and abort `perform_retrieve` before it reaches `fetch_http`, so the intended fallback to direct HTTP retrieval would not run while feed polling is enabled and failing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — <%- end if %>` is a Ruby syntax error (verified: ERB compile fails with "unexpected ';'"), so the primary third-party endpoint GET /embed/best 500s on every request.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:1 — embed.js/embed.css are never added to `config.assets.precompile`, so the file third-party blogs are meant to `<script src>` has no stable, servable URL in production.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new standalone asset entrypoints `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` and `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss`. The new layout `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` explicitly does `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`, which in a typical Rails production setup (assets.compile=false) requires `embed.css` to be precompiled as its own manifest. Similarly, `embed.js` appears intended to be loaded directly by third-party sites via a `<script src=...>` URL, but it is not required by any existing manifest in the diff. The diff does not add either asset to any precompile list/manifest, so these assets would not be generated/servable in production by default.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — request.referer` is interpolated raw (full URL incl. path/query) into a JS single-quoted postMessage targetOrigin; any apostrophe or quote in the embedding page URL breaks the resize protocol for that embedder.
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same core problem: `request.referer` is inserted into a JavaScript single-quoted string without escaping. The candidate emphasizes broken behavior when quotes appear in the URL, but that same unescaped interpolation is what enables breaking out of the string and potentially injecting script (XSS) as described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — raw_html posts store unsanitized source HTML into `cooked`, breaking the invariant every existing consumer of `cooked`/`excerpt` relies on (Ember app, posts JSON API, digest emails, RSS).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` and changes `Post#cook` to return `raw` unchanged when `cook_method == :raw_html` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and passes HTML content from RSS/Readability directly into `raw` (skip_validations: true). That means the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline is bypassed and whatever HTML is in `raw` will be treated as `cooked` output for these posts, which can break the implicit expectation that `cooked` contains already-sanitized, safe HTML for all downstream consumers (rendering, excerpts, APIs, emails, RSS). Nothing in the diff applies sanitization to the imported HTML (only a limited Readability tag/attribute allowlist in `import_remote`, and no sanitization for RSS `i.content`), so XSS/unsafe HTML is a concrete risk introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15 — embed_url` is matched byte-exactly with no normalization, so trailing-slash/scheme/query differences between the blog's `discourseEmbedUrl` and the feed `<link>` yield duplicate topics or a permanently "Loading" iframe.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff stores and looks up `TopicEmbed` records by exact string equality on `embed_url` (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url)` in `import` and `topic_id_for_embed`). There is no normalization/canonicalization (scheme, trailing slash, query params, redirects, etc.), and the DB enforces uniqueness on the raw string via a unique index on `embed_url`. Since the iframe requests `embed_url` from `discourseEmbedUrl` (JS) while feed polling imports from `i.link`/`i.id`, different-but-equivalent URLs will not match, causing `topic_id_for_embed` to return nil and `TopicRetriever` to fetch/import again, creating a duplicate topic for the same page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative `//cdn.host/x` and rewrites it to `http://blog/cdn.host/x`; relative URLs not starting with `/` are left to resolve against the Discourse host.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, links/images are rewritten only when `href/src.start_with?('/')`. This will also match protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.host/x`, and the code then strips leading slashes and prefixes the embed page’s host (`prefix`), producing `http://<embed-host>/cdn.host/x`, which is incorrect. Additionally, other relative URLs (e.g., `images/x`, `../x`, `./x`) are not rewritten at all and would resolve relative to the Discourse host when the HTML is served from Discourse, which is likely wrong for imported content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — The loading page reloads unconditionally every 30s forever and each reload re-enqueues a retrieve job, so an unresolvable embed_url turns every reader's browser into a permanent poller against the forum.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) returns nil, it unconditionally does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. The loading template (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb) includes a JS `setTimeout` that calls `document.location.reload()` every 30000ms with no stop condition. Therefore, for an embed_url that never becomes resolvable/importable, the iframe will repeatedly hit /embed/best and each request will enqueue another retrieve_topic job. While TopicRetriever has a 60s throttle on *execution*, it does not prevent repeated job enqueues, so readers can continuously generate background jobs and requests indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — embed_url` is `t.string` (varchar(255) under the Rails 4.0 PG adapter) with a unique index; article URLs longer than 255 chars will raise on insert.

adjudication.rationale: In 20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb, `embed_url` is defined as `t.string` with no explicit `limit`, which under Rails 4 with PostgreSQL maps to `character varying(255)`. The diff also adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true` and multiple code paths (`TopicEmbed.import`, `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, RSS polling, retriever) that store full article URLs without any length validation/truncation. If an embed URL exceeds 255 characters, PostgreSQL will reject the insert/update with a value-too-long error, causing runtime failures and preventing embeds from being created/updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:25 — The distinct `Discourse::InvalidAccess` messages ("embeddable host not set" vs "invalid referer host") are discarded by the shared rescue handler, so neither embedders nor operators can distinguish the two 403s.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the `rescue` clause only catches `URI::InvalidURIError` and re-raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess.new('invalid referer host')`. The earlier `raise Discourse::InvalidAccess.new('embeddable host not set')` is not inside a rescue that would replace/discard it, so the two conditions remain distinguishable via their exception messages. Only invalid/parse errors of the referer are normalized to the “invalid referer host” message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9 — ensure_embeddable` runs before `params.require(:embed_url)`, so a missing required param returns 403 rather than the 400 the spec claims; the error contract for embedders is undefined.

adjudication.rationale: It’s true that `ensure_embeddable` runs before `best` (and thus before `params.require(:embed_url)`), so a request missing `embed_url` *could* fail in the before_filter first (e.g., because `request.referer` is nil/invalid) rather than raising `ActionController::ParameterMissing`. However, the proposed finding’s key claim (“returns 403 rather than the 400 the spec claims”) is not grounded in the diff: the spec `it "is 404 without an embed_url"` only asserts `response.should_not be_success` and does not assert 400/403/404. Also, if the referer passes, the action will still hit `params.require(:embed_url)` and produce the normal missing-parameter error. This is more about undefined/desired error semantics than a clear defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:24 — PostCreator#create returns the unsaved @post after an internal ActiveRecord::Rollback (spam/validation), so post.present? is true while post.id and post.topic_id are nil and TopicEmbed.create! then violates the NOT NULL columns

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows TopicEmbed.import checking only `post.present?` before calling `TopicEmbed.create!` with `post.topic_id`/`post.id`, which would indeed break if `creator.create` ever returned a non-nil, non-persisted Post. However, the proposed finding’s key claim—`PostCreator#create` returning an unsaved `@post` after an internal `ActiveRecord::Rollback` (e.g., spam/validation failure)—depends on PostCreator implementation details not shown in this diff. Since that behavior is not verifiable from the provided changes, the finding is speculative as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 — a TopicEmbed row whose topic was deleted makes TopicView raise NotFound on every request forever, since perform_retrieve bails out whenever the embed row exists and nothing removes the stale row

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `EmbedController#best` uses `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` and, if it returns an id, immediately constructs `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` with no guard that the topic still exists. A stale `topic_embeds` row (possible because `topic_embeds` has no foreign keys and the model has no `dependent: :destroy` on `Topic`) can therefore cause `TopicView` to raise (e.g., NotFound) on every request. It also becomes self-perpetuating because `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` begins with `return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`, so the presence of the stale row prevents any re-retrieval/recreation path from running, and nothing in the diff cleans up such stale rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — switching topic creation to TopicEmbed.import_remote drops created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), so every imported Disqus thread is now dated at import time

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` from creating the first post via `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), ...)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicEmbed.import` do not pass a `created_at` option into `PostCreator`, and `PostCreator` only sets `post.created_at` when `@opts[:created_at]` is present. Therefore the imported thread’s initial post/topic will be timestamped at import time instead of the Disqus thread’s original `created_at`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — the loading page is cached for 1 minute for anonymous users but reloads itself after 30 seconds, so the first reload is served the cached loading page instead of the topic

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is executed regardless of whether a topic exists or the `loading` template is rendered. The `loading.html.erb` page calls `document.location.reload()` after 30 seconds. With a 60s cache lifetime on the loading response (same URL including `embed_url`), the browser/proxy can legitimately serve the cached loading page on that first reload, preventing the request from reaching the server to detect that the topic has since been created. This creates a real correctness/UX bug (at minimum delaying showing the topic until cache expiry).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:59 — the port is appended based on the number alone, so http://host:443 loses its port (and https://host:80 too), producing wrong absolute URLs

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, the prefix adds ":#{uri.port}" only if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443. This check ignores the URL scheme, so a non-default port that happens to be 80 or 443 for the given scheme is dropped (e.g., "http://host:443" yields prefix "http://host"; "https://host:80" yields "https://host"). That would produce incorrect absolute URLs when the embed URL uses these cross-scheme ports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — Edits an already-shipped migration to add `force: true`, which silently DROPs an existing top_topics table (and all its rows) on any re-run, while being a no-op for deployments that already recorded this version.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. That means if this migration is ever re-run (e.g., on rollback/re-migrate, db:reset, or if the table exists but the migration version isn’t recorded), it can silently destroy any existing `top_topics` data instead of failing loudly. This risky behavior is introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` is destructive DDL: a re-run or schema reload silently drops the table and all embed mappings instead of failing loudly.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which instructs Rails to drop the table if it already exists and recreate it. That is destructive DDL: if the migration is ever re-run against a database that already has `topic_embeds` (e.g., due to a manual rerun, a botched deployment, or divergent schema state), it will silently delete all existing embed mappings instead of failing with “table already exists”. This behavior is directly implied by `force: true` in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — add_column` with a non-null DEFAULT on `posts` forces a full table rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on PostgreSQL of this era, blocking all post reads/writes for the duration on a large site.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds migration `20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb` with `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions common at the time this code was written (pre-11), adding a non-null column with a DEFAULT typically rewrites the entire table and requires an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the duration, blocking reads/writes to `posts` on large installs. This is directly implied by the migration as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — embed_url` is an unbounded `t.string` (varchar(255)) but stores arbitrary RSS/Atom item links with no length validation in TopicEmbed, so a >255-char URL raises StatementInvalid and aborts the whole feed poll.

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds.embed_url` as `t.string` with no explicit `limit`, which in Rails maps to a VARCHAR with the adapter’s default limit (commonly 255). The model only validates presence of `embed_url` (no length validation) and `TopicEmbed.import` persists via `TopicEmbed.create!` using the full URL from RSS/Atom (`i.link` / `i.id`) with no truncation. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the import runs inside an `.each` with no rescue, so an over-255 URL would raise during insert/update and abort the whole poll job (and `sidekiq_options retry: false` means it won’t retry).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — Deploy-ordering hazard: `Post#cook` reads `cook_method` unconditionally, so any app instance running before migration 20131219203905 completes raises NoMethodError on every cook.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Post#cook` to call `cook_method` on every cook (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). The `cook_method` attribute only exists after the new migration `20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb` adds the `posts.cook_method` column. If code is deployed to an app server before that migration has run (a common rolling deploy scenario), ActiveRecord will not have an attribute method for `cook_method`, so calling it will raise `NoMethodError` during cooking/rendering of posts. This is a real deploy-ordering hazard introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:24 — Check-then-insert against the new unique index on `embed_url` with no model-level uniqueness validation: concurrent PollFeed and TopicRetriever runs raise an unrescued RecordNotUnique.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic "find then create" (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then `TopicEmbed.create!`) while the migration adds a **unique index** on `topic_embeds.embed_url`. If two workers/processes (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` iterating items and `TopicRetriever`/`RetrieveTopic` fetching the same URL) call `import` concurrently for the same `embed_url`, both can observe `embed.blank?` and then one `create!` will hit the unique index and raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. There is no rescue/retry logic and no model-level uniqueness validation in the diff, so this exception would be unhandled and can fail the job/request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4 — topic_id`/`post_id` are NOT NULL with no foreign key or dependent-destroy, so deleting a topic/post leaves an orphan row whose unique `embed_url` permanently blocks re-import and makes `embed.post` nil in TopicEmbed.import.

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds` with `topic_id` and `post_id` declared NOT NULL and a unique index on `embed_url`, but the diff adds no foreign keys and the `TopicEmbed` model’s `belongs_to :topic` / `belongs_to :post` has no `dependent:` cleanup from the owning `Topic`/`Post` side. If a `Topic` or `Post` is deleted without also deleting the corresponding `topic_embeds` row, the unique `embed_url` row can remain and `TopicEmbed.import` will take the `else` branch (because the row exists), do `post = embed.post` (which can be nil if the post is gone), and then call `PostRevisor.new(post)` / `revisor.revise!`, which would error. Additionally, the stale unique `embed_url` row prevents re-creating a fresh embed mapping for the same URL. This is a real correctness risk present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:11 — No index on `topic_id` or `post_id` despite `belongs_to :topic`/`belongs_to :post` and lookups/cleanup by those columns.

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `create_topic_embeds`, the only index added is `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`; there is indeed no index on `topic_id` or `post_id`. However, within this diff all shown queries against `TopicEmbed` are by `embed_url` (e.g., `where(embed_url: ...)`, `topic_id_for_embed`), not by `topic_id` or `post_id`. The claim about "lookups/cleanup by those columns" is not verifiable from the diff, so this is at most a potential performance improvement rather than a clear defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — <%- end if %>` is a Ruby syntax error (verified: ERB compile fails), so the embed view can never render.
matched_golden_ids: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that the ERB/Ruby block is incorrectly closed with `end if`, which is invalid syntax and prevents the template from rendering; the fix is to use `end` to close the `if` block.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:4 — New top-level assets `embed.css.scss` and `embed.js` are referenced/served directly but no precompile list is updated in this diff, so production will raise "asset is not precompiled".

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new standalone stylesheet `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` and the new layout `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` includes it via `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`, which in production resolves to `embed.css`. Under Rails/Sprockets defaults, only `application.js`/`application.css` (and a limited default glob) are precompiled; additional top-level CSS/JS entrypoints typically must be added to `config.assets.precompile`. This diff does not add `embed.css` (or the new standalone `embed.js`) to any precompile list/manifest, so it can realistically lead to “asset is not precompiled” errors in production when rendering the embed layout.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — An already-committed migration is edited to add `force: true`, which silently drops an existing `top_topics` table (and its data) on re-run instead of failing loudly.

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration (20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails/ActiveRecord, `force: true` will drop an existing table and recreate it instead of raising an error if the table already exists. If this migration is run against a DB where `top_topics` already exists but the migration is not marked as applied (or during certain rebuild/redo workflows), it can silently destroy existing `top_topics` data rather than failing loudly. This is a concrete behavior change introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — The `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` comparison is duplicated in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` (lib/topic_retriever.rb:15) with different blank/nil handling; the two copies will drift.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does contain two separate host checks: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` rejects when `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?` and compares the *referer* host, while `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` compares the *embed_url* host and treats `nil`/blank implicitly as mismatch (`nil != "host"` -> true). This is duplicated logic in a broad sense, but it is not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff: both paths currently reject missing/blank settings and mismatched hosts, and they intentionally validate different inputs (referer vs embed_url). The claim about future drift is speculative rather than a concrete bug/security/correctness problem present now.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — The layout re-derives the postMessage target origin from raw `request.referer` (a third copy of the host trust logic) and HTML-escapes it into a JS string literal, so quoting/`&` in the referer corrupts the value.

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb the code does `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>');`. `request.referer` is a full URL (often includes path/query), but `postMessage`’s `targetOrigin` is expected to be an origin (scheme+host+port) or `*`; supplying a full URL can cause the message to be rejected or throw in some browsers. Additionally, `<%= %>` applies HTML escaping, which is not correct for a JS string context inside a `<script>` tag; characters like `&` become `&` (changing the string and breaking origin matching) and quotes may be entity-escaped then decoded by the HTML parser back into quotes, corrupting/breaking the JS string. So the finding describes a real defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — The model builds presentation/attribution HTML (`<hr><small>Imported from...`) and destructively appends it to the caller's `contents` string, mutating an argument owned by the feed job.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the code does `contents << "\n<hr>..."`, which mutates the String object passed in by the caller (Ruby `<<` appends in-place). This is directly verifiable in the diff and can cause unintended side effects if the caller expects `contents` to remain unchanged or reuses it elsewhere (e.g., for logging, hashing, retries). The attribution HTML also being constructed in the model is present, but the concrete defect is the destructive mutation of an argument.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — TopicRetriever` instantiates and runs the scheduled `Jobs::PollFeed` inline, coupling a single-URL request-path retrieval to the whole-feed poller and to job-class internals.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve explicitly does `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. This means a retrieval for a single `@embed_url` will synchronously run the entire feed poller (network fetch + iterating/importing all items) rather than enqueueing a job or handling only the requested URL. This is a concrete coupling to the scheduled job class’ implementation and can cause unnecessary work/latency for each retrieve attempt (even though it’s typically triggered via Jobs::RetrieveTopic).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — Switching the importer to `TopicEmbed.import_remote` drops the previous `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`, so imported Disqus topics silently lose their original creation dates.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the old code created the topic via PostCreator with `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`. The new code replaces that with `post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` only forwards `opts[:title]` (or doc.title) into `TopicEmbed.import`, and `TopicEmbed.import` constructs `PostCreator.new(user, title: ..., raw: ..., skip_validations: true, cook_method: ...)` without any `created_at` option. Therefore the imported topic/post timestamps will default to “now”, losing the original Disqus creation dates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:116 — The `--category` CLI option and its `Category.where(...)` lookup were deleted, regressing the importer's ability to place imported topics in a category.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the Thor option `method_option :category` and all related logic that looked up `Category.where(name: options[:category])` and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator.new(...)`. The import path now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and neither this call nor `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicEmbed.import` accept or set a category. As a result, Disqus imports can no longer be directed into a specified category via CLI and will fall back to the default category behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18 — The "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" examples stub only one setting while the others stay falsy, so they pass vacuously and would still pass if the guard were removed.

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute, poll_feed is only called if all three conditions are true: feed_polling_enabled?, feed_polling_url.present?, and embed_by_username.present?. In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the "requires feed_polling_url" example only stubs feed_polling_url to nil and does not stub feed_polling_enabled? to true or embed_by_username to a present value; given the default setting in config/site_settings.yml sets feed_polling_enabled: false, the guard will fail regardless of feed_polling_url, so the expectation `poll_feed` is never called passes vacuously. adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — perform_retrieve runs the entire hourly feed poll inline (full feed download, parse and import of every item) on each embed cache miss, so N distinct missing URLs cause N full-feed imports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — SimpleRSS.parse open(url)` pulls the whole feed into memory with no size cap, read timeout, or item limit, and `rss.items.each` then imports every entry unbounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url).read` reads an arbitrary remote page fully into memory and hands it to Readability/Nokogiri with no timeout or size limit, pinning a Sidekiq worker.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Every anonymous hit on a not-yet-imported embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job (throttling happens only inside the job), so a public unauthenticated endpoint can flood the Sidekiq queue.

There is no rate limit/throttle before enqueuing. The only throttling shown in the diff is inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, which is invoked later when the enqueued `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` runs. This means repeated requests for the same not-yet-imported `embed_url` will enqueue many Sidekiq jobs, even if each job later no-ops due to the Redis throttle. Since the route `get 'embed/best'` is public and `current_user` can be nil, this is a queue-flood/DoS vector (the referer check is header-based and does not prevent a client from sending many requests).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute` marks the response publicly cacheable while both the authorization decision and the rendered postMessage origin depend on `Referer`, with no `Vary: Referer` set.

db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — add_column with `null: false, default: 1` on the posts table forces a full table rewrite under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on the largest table in the schema.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `AddCookMethodToPosts` that executes `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions commonly used with Rails apps of this era, adding a column with both a non-NULL default and `null: false` generally rewrites the whole table and takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the duration. Since `posts` is typically one of the largest tables, this is a real deploy-time risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — The loading page hard-reloads every 30s with no backoff or attempt cap, so every parked blog reader generates a sustained stream of embed requests and job enqueues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — feed_key` (the last-modified cache key) is computed but never used, so every poll refetches and re-hashes the entire feed instead of doing a conditional GET.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the method `feed_key` (lines ~17-19) computes a Redis-style cache key based on the feed URL, but it is never referenced anywhere in the job. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open(...)` / `SimpleRSS.parse` are unrescued, so any DNS/connect/timeout/HTTP-error or malformed-feed exception propagates out of the scheduled job and the whole poll is lost

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, poll_feed does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no rescue/handling around `open` (open-uri) or `SimpleRSS.parse`. Both can raise (network/DNS/timeout/HTTP errors, invalid URI, malformed feed). Since PollFeed is a scheduled Sidekiq job and sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, any exception will cause the job execution to abort and not retry, losing that polling cycle. This behavior is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — no per-item rescue in the item loop: one bad entry (nil title/content, invalid URL, PostCreator failure) aborts the batch and every subsequent item in the feed is skipped

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `rss.items.each do |i| ... content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) ... TopicEmbed.import(...) end` with no per-item `rescue`. If any feed item has `i.content == nil` (or otherwise not a String), calling `.scrub` will raise (e.g., `NoMethodError`), which will abort `poll_feed` and skip all remaining items. The diff contains no guards (`to_s`, presence checks) or exception handling inside the loop, so the batch can be terminated by a single bad entry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — no open/read timeout on the outbound feed fetch (open-uri inherits Net::HTTP's per-read defaults), so a slow-drip or hanging feed host can pin a Sidekiq worker indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the feed is fetched via `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` (or higher-level total timeout) options passed to `open-uri`. With `Net::HTTP`-backed reads, a server that never completes the response (or slow-drips data frequently enough to avoid per-read timeouts) can keep this call blocked for an unbounded duration, tying up the scheduled Sidekiq worker. This risk is introduced by the diff and is directly verifiable from the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:12 — sidekiq_options retry: false` on a job whose main work is a network fetch means any transient network blip discards that hour's import with no retry and no alerting

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added scheduled job `Jobs::PollFeed`, the code explicitly sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` and then performs a network fetch via `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no error handling. If `open-uri` raises due to a transient network/feed issue, Sidekiq will not retry this execution, so that polling run is effectively skipped until the next hourly recurrence. The "no retry" aspect is directly verifiable in the diff; explicit alerting behavior is not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — feed_key` is computed but never referenced anywhere; the intended If-Modified-Since/conditional-GET short-circuit is unimplemented, so every hourly run refetches and re-processes the entire feed

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` (lines ~17-19) computes and memoizes a Redis key based on `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`, but it is never called from `execute`, `poll_feed`, or anywhere else in the diff. The actual `poll_feed` implementation always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all `rss.items` every run, with no use of `feed_key` (or any other mechanism) to short-circuit based on feed modification time/etag/previous hash. So the “computed but never referenced; refetches and reprocesses the feed each run” part is directly supported by the diff (the conditional-GET intent is inferred but consistent with the unused `feed_key`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — the IO returned by `open` is never closed, leaking a file descriptor/tempfile on every hourly run and every inline invocation from TopicRetriever

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the code does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` without using a block. With `open-uri`, calling `open(...)` without a block returns an IO/Tempfile-like object that the caller is responsible for closing. SimpleRSS.parse will read from the IO but does not inherently guarantee closing it, so in a long-running process (Sidekiq) this can accumulate open file descriptors/tempfiles across hourly runs and inline invocations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — String#scrub` requires Ruby >= 2.1; on the Ruby 2.0 runtime of this era this raises NoMethodError only at runtime, never at load/test time
app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url).read` in `import_remote` has no timeout and no rescue, so a slow or dead embeddable host hangs or crashes the RetrieveTopic job and the disqus importer

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote, the code does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` with `require 'open-uri'` used elsewhere and no `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` options passed to `open`, and no exception handling around the network fetch. If the remote host is slow/unresponsive, `open(url).read` can block for a long time, and if it errors (timeouts, DNS, connection reset, etc.) it will raise and bubble up. This method is called from TopicRetriever#fetch_http (used by Jobs::RetrieveTopic) and from the disqus importer task, both of which do not rescue around `import_remote`, so the job/task can fail due to network issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:1 — file calls `open` (open-uri) and `Digest::SHA1` without requiring `open-uri`/`digest/sha1`; only poll_feed.rb requires them, so under dev autoloading `import_remote` can reach Kernel#open and fail with Errno::ENOENT

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb`, `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` but the file never `require`s `open-uri`. Without `open-uri` loaded elsewhere, Ruby will use `Kernel#open` (treating the URL like a filename) and will raise `Errno::ENOENT` for `http://...`. The model also uses `Digest::SHA1.hexdigest` in `.import` without requiring `digest/sha1`. Although other files (e.g. `poll_feed.rb`) require these stdlibs, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` is invoked from other entry points (e.g. the Disqus thor task) that don’t add those requires, so the missing requires are a real defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — post = embed.post` can be nil when the post was deleted but the topic_embed row remains; `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` then raises NoMethodError and kills the whole import batch

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then, if the SHA changed, immediately calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` / `revise!` without guarding against `post` being nil. Although `topic_embeds.post_id` is `null: false`, there is no foreign key or other enforcement shown in the diff, and `belongs_to :post` will return `nil` if the referenced post row is deleted while the `topic_embeds` row remains. In that case, `PostRevisor.new(nil)` (and subsequent method calls) would raise and abort the import operation. The nil case is not handled anywhere in this method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:20 — check-then-create on `embed_url` races the unique index added by the migration; concurrent PollFeed/RetrieveTopic runs raise an unrescued ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique that aborts the batch

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, later does `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`. Two concurrent executions (e.g., PollFeed and/or RetrieveTopic importing the same URL) can both observe no row and then both attempt `create!`; the loser will raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique due to the unique index. There is no rescue around this in TopicEmbed.import, Jobs::PollFeed, or Jobs::RetrieveTopic, so the exception would bubble up and abort the job/batch iteration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:57 — URI(url)` in `absolutize_urls` can raise URI::InvalidURIError for URLs with spaces/unicode that still pass the `^https?://` guard, aborting the import loop

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls(url, contents)`, the code does `uri = URI(url)` with no `rescue`. The only validation before calling it is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` in `TopicEmbed.import`, which allows strings like `"http://example.com/a b"` or other characters that still match the prefix but cause `URI.parse`/`URI()` to raise `URI::InvalidURIError`. Since `PollFeed` and `TopicRetriever.import_remote` both ultimately call `TopicEmbed.import(...)` and then `absolutize_urls(...)`, a single malformed-but-prefixed URL would raise and can break the import flow (e.g., aborting the feed loop/job).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — contents <<` mutates the caller's string in place, so the "Imported from" footer is appended to the caller's object and a frozen input string raises RuntimeError

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the line `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends to the passed-in `contents` String in place. This introduces an observable side effect for callers (their String gets modified), and if a caller ever passes a frozen String (or otherwise immutable string-like), `<<` will raise (FrozenError/RuntimeError depending on Ruby). The mutation is directly present in the diff and not mitigated (e.g., by `contents = contents.dup`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs the full feed poll (network fetch plus N topic imports) synchronously inside every RetrieveTopic job, unthrottled and racing with the hourly scheduled run

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. `Jobs::PollFeed#execute` can synchronously run `poll_feed`, which does `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (network fetch) and iterates `rss.items.each` importing/updating potentially many topics. This happens inside every TopicRetriever run (e.g., via the RetrieveTopic job triggered by EmbedController when no embed exists), and TopicRetriever’s throttle (`retrieved_recently?`) is per `@embed_url`, not per feed URL, so multiple distinct embed URLs can each trigger a full feed poll. There is no locking or rate-limiting around PollFeed itself, so it can also run concurrently with the scheduled hourly PollFeed job.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — non-atomic `setnx` then `expire`: if the process dies between the two calls the `retrieved:` key never expires and that embed_url is throttled out permanently

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only afterward given a TTL via `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two separate Redis commands; if the process/thread crashes or is interrupted after SETNX succeeds but before EXPIRE runs, the key will remain without an expiry and future calls will treat the URL as "retrieved recently" forever (permanent throttling for that embed_url). This is a real correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:17 — job has no rescue around TopicRetriever's network/parse work and no retry override, so a permanently unreachable embed URL is re-fetched ~25 times over weeks by Sidekiq's default backoff

adjudication.rationale: The new job `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb) calls `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve` with no `rescue` and no `sidekiq_options`/retry override. `TopicRetriever` can reach `fetch_http`, which calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` (network I/O) and HTML parsing via `ruby-readability`/Nokogiri—both can raise exceptions (timeouts, DNS failures, invalid responses, parse errors). With no handling, any such exception will cause the job to fail and be retried under Sidekiq’s default retry behavior (commonly 25 retries with exponential backoff), repeatedly re-attempting an unreachable URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — RetrieveTopic is enqueued unconditionally on every cache miss, so a page that can never be fetched produces an unbounded stream of duplicate jobs (one per visitor per reload)

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) returns nil it always calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url) and renders the loading page. The loading view auto-reloads every 30 seconds, so for an embed_url that never results in a TopicEmbed (e.g., fetch fails/404/timeout), each reload/visit will enqueue another RetrieveTopic job. While TopicRetriever has a Redis throttle that prevents repeated *work* within 60s, it does not prevent repeated *enqueuing*, so the queue can accumulate an unbounded number of duplicate jobs over time (one per visitor per reload) until the embed is successfully created (which in this scenario never happens).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — the 30s `document.location.reload()` has no attempt cap or terminal error state, so a permanently unfetchable embed loops forever, re-enqueuing jobs and hammering the remote host

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` exists it unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `embed/loading`. The `loading.html.erb` view then does `setTimeout(function(){ document.location.reload(); }, 30000);` with no cap or fallback, so a never-resolving embed will cause infinite reloads and repeated requests. Each reload hits `#best` again and will enqueue another `retrieve_topic` job, so the system can be spammed with redundant jobs; the remote-host hammering aspect is somewhat mitigated by `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` throttling (60s) for non-staff, but the infinite loop and job re-enqueueing are directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 — if the embedded topic is deleted the TopicEmbed row still resolves to its id and `TopicView.new` raises Discourse::NotFound, so the iframe 404s permanently instead of degrading to the loading/create path

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the branch decision is solely `if topic_id` from `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)`, which does `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first`. If a `TopicEmbed` row remains after its associated `Topic` is deleted (no `dependent: :destroy`, no FK/cascade in the migration), `topic_id_for_embed` will still return a non-nil id. The controller will then call `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` and will not enqueue `:retrieve_topic` or render `loading`. If `TopicView.new` raises when the topic doesn’t exist (typical behavior), this produces a permanent error path rather than falling back to the loading/recreate flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — adding `force: true` to an already-shipped migration will DROP an existing populated top_topics table if that migration is ever re-run or replayed

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before creating it. If this migration is ever executed against a database that already has a populated `top_topics` table (e.g., on re-run after rollback, reset, or replaying migrations in an environment), it can destroy existing data instead of failing safely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` silently drops and recreates the table (losing embed mappings) on any re-run instead of failing loudly

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and then recreate it, which can silently delete existing `topic_embeds` data if the migration is ever run against a database where the table is present (e.g., inconsistent state, manual pre-creation, or other nonstandard migration flows). This behavior is directly implied by the code in the diff and is a real data-loss risk compared to failing loudly when the table already exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:11 — document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` is never null-checked, so on a host page without that element the script throws and breaks the host page's other JS

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the script does `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then unconditionally calls `comments.appendChild(iframe);`. If the host page does not contain an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be `null` and `appendChild` will throw a `TypeError`, aborting the script. There is no null-check or fallback in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — iframe height is posted once from `window.onload` with no resize/mutation handling, so late-loading images or content leave the embed permanently clipped

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` the resize message is sent from `window.onload`, which fires only after the embedded document (including images and other subresources present in the initial HTML) has finished loading. Given the diff, the embed content is server-rendered (`embed/best.html.erb`) and doesn’t introduce any dynamic DOM mutations after load, so the claim that “late-loading images or content leave the embed permanently clipped” is not directly verifiable from this change. While the height could become stale on later viewport changes, that’s not what the finding asserts and isn’t clearly a defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18 — the "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" tests never stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to true, so they pass vacuously and assert nothing

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute, poll_feed only runs if all three conditions are true: feed_polling_enabled?, feed_polling_url.present?, and embed_by_username.present?. In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the "requires feed_polling_url" test only stubs feed_polling_url to nil (and does not stub feed_polling_enabled? to true), and the "requires embed_by_username" test only stubs embed_by_username to nil (and does not stub feed_polling_enabled? to true). Since the new site setting feed_polling_enabled defaults to false in config/site_settings.yml, these tests will typically pass because the first condition is false, not because the missing URL/username is being enforced—i.e., they can pass vacuously and don’t actually verify the intended behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:44 — the test stubs `TopicRetriever.new` but the controller now enqueues a Sidekiq job, so this expectation only holds if jobs run inline in the test env

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no existing embed is found (topic_id nil), the controller calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`. It does not instantiate `TopicRetriever` directly. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` expects `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)` during the request. That expectation will not be satisfied by the controller code as shown in the diff; it would only happen inside the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` job when/if it runs, not during the controller action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — the item URL is interpolated into a single-quoted `href` attribute without escaping, so a feed link like `http://x' onmouseover='alert(1)` injects arbitrary attributes/HTML into every imported (raw_html) post

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In TopicEmbed.import, the code appends HTML containing the unescaped URL: `"#{url}"`. The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which allows quotes/spaces after the scheme (e.g. `http://x' onmouseover='alert(1)`). Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, Post#cook returns `raw` directly (skipping the cooking/sanitization pipeline), and the embed view renders `raw post.cooked`. This makes attribute/HTML injection via a malicious feed/link value directly exploitable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 — raw post.cooked` renders post bodies unescaped in a page served with `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL`, so raw_html-imported content executes in the embedding page's iframe

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds support for importing posts with `cook_method == :raw_html` (Post#cook returns `raw` directly, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline). `TopicEmbed.import` and `Jobs::PollFeed` feed raw HTML content into posts (PollFeed does not sanitize; it just `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`), and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). That means any HTML (including potentially `<script>` or event handlers) in imported content will be emitted unescaped and execute in the iframe (Discourse origin). The controller also sets `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL`, so this executable content is readily embeddable on the configured host. Overall, this is a real XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses Kernel#open semantics on an admin-settable string with no scheme validation, allowing `|command` process spawning and file:/ftp: reads (admin -> server RCE/SSRF)
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to PollFeed using Ruby's `open` on `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url` without validating the URL/scheme, enabling arbitrary fetching (SSRF). The candidate additionally mentions `Kernel#open` command/file/ftp vectors, but it still identifies the same core issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — postMessage origin validation is a substring test (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`) rather than an exact origin comparison, so a lookalike origin that is a substring of the forum URL (e.g. `https://forum.example.co` inside `https://forum.example.com/`) is accepted, and `e.source` is never checked
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that the postMessage origin validation uses a substring/indexOf check instead of an exact origin match, allowing lookalike/malicious domains to bypass validation (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com or similar substring cases). Candidate adds an extra issue about e.source, but the core issue matches the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — the response is marked cacheable for 1 minute although it is rendered per-user via `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user)` and access-gated on the Referer header, with no `Vary: Referer` and no anonymous-only guard, so a shared cache can serve one user's view (and bypass the referer gate) to others

spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18 — Vacuous test: `feed_polling_enabled?` is never stubbed on (site setting defaults to false), so `execute` short-circuits on the first condition and the test passes even if the `feed_polling_url` guard were deleted

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute, poll_feed runs only if `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? && SiteSetting.feed_polling_url.present? && SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?`. In `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, the test "requires feed_polling_url" stubs only `feed_polling_url` to nil and never stubs `feed_polling_enabled?` to true. Given the default in `config/site_settings.yml` is `feed_polling_enabled: false`, `execute` will short-circuit on the first condition, so the expectation that `poll_feed` is never called would still pass even if the `feed_polling_url` check were removed. The same issue applies to the "requires embed_by_username" test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:24 — Vacuous test: same problem — `feed_polling_enabled?` defaults to false, so the `embed_by_username.present?` guard is never actually exercised

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute, poll_feed only runs when all three conditions are true: feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?. In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the tests "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" only stub feed_polling_url or embed_by_username to nil, but do not stub feed_polling_enabled? to true. Given the default in config/site_settings.yml is feed_polling_enabled: false, those tests will pass because the first condition fails, so they never actually exercise the intended guard (feed_polling_url.present? / embed_by_username.present?). This makes those tests effectively vacuous with respect to the stated requirement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:24 — No test for the security-relevant case: a referer whose host does NOT match `embeddable_host` (only nil referer is covered), nor for a malformed referer exercising the `URI::InvalidURIError` rescue in `ensure_embeddable

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the tests cover: missing embed_url, missing embeddable_host, and a nil referer ("raises an error with no referer"). The controller’s ensure_embeddable method additionally enforces that URI(request.referer||'').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host and rescues URI::InvalidURIError to raise InvalidAccess. There is no test exercising (a) a non-nil referer whose host differs from embeddable_host, nor (b) a malformed referer that triggers the URI::InvalidURIError rescue path. This is directly verifiable from the diff and is security-relevant logic that is currently untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:48 — Controller spec never calls `render_views` and `TopicView.expects(:new)` returns nil, so no spec ever renders app/views/embed/*; the stray `<%- end if %>` at app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 (an ERB/Ruby syntax error) cannot be caught by any test

spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:39 — The re-import test asserts only `post.cooked =~ /new contents/`; it never asserts that no second Topic/TopicEmbed was created (`TopicEmbed.count == 1`, same topic_id/post_id), so a regression that duplicates topics on every feed poll would still pass

adjudication.rationale: The spec at spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb indeed only checks `post.cooked` contains “new contents” on re-import and does not assert `TopicEmbed.count == 1` or that the same post/topic was reused. However, the diff’s implementation already prevents duplicate `topic_embeds` for the same URL via `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and a DB unique index on `embed_url`; creating a second topic/embed for the same URL would either not happen or would raise and roll back. So the proposed finding is a test-coverage improvement suggestion, not a real, verifiable defect introduced by this diff, and its “duplicates topics on every feed poll would still pass” claim doesn’t realistically apply given the uniqueness constraint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:32 — The only "valid host" tests stub out both `perform_retrieve` and `retrieved_recently?`, so they verify mocks only: the redis throttle (setnx/expire, `no_throttle` opt), the existing-embed short-circuit, the inline `Jobs::PollFeed` call and `fetch_http` user lookup have zero coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `TopicRetriever` with nontrivial behavior (host validation, redis throttle via `setnx`/`expire` and `no_throttle`, short-circuit when an embed already exists, optional inline `Jobs::PollFeed` execution, and `fetch_http` user lookup + `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). The new spec `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` only asserts whether `perform_retrieve` is called or not, and in the “valid host” examples it stubs `retrieved_recently?` and mocks `perform_retrieve`, so none of the internal logic in `retrieved_recently?` or `perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http` is exercised. There are no other new tests in the diff that cover these branches, so the finding about mock-only coverage and zero coverage for those behaviors is verifiably accurate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:31 — poll_feed` is stubbed out in every example, so the entire feed body (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:24-38) is untested: missing user, `i.link` blank/non-http fallback to `i.id`, and `i.content.scrub` which NoMethodErrors on RSS 2.0 items whose `content` is nil

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, poll_feed does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks `content` (common in many RSS 2.0 feeds where `description` is used instead), `i.content` can be nil and `nil.scrub` would raise NoMethodError. The added spec/spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only tests gating logic in `execute` and explicitly expects `poll_feed` to be called/not called; it never exercises the `poll_feed` body, so this nil-content case (and other branches like link fallback to `i.id`) is indeed untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8 — "is 404 without an embed_url" passes for the wrong reason: `embeddable_host` is blank by default so `ensure_embeddable` raises before `params.require(:embed_url)` runs, and `should_not be_success` cannot tell the difference; the missing-param path is untested

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController, `before_filter :ensure_embeddable` runs before `best`, and `ensure_embeddable` raises immediately when `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?`. The diff sets the default `embeddable_host` to '' in `config/site_settings.yml`, so in `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` the example `it "is 404 without an embed_url" do get :best ... end` will fail the request due to the blank embeddable_host (before `params.require(:embed_url)` is reached). Since the assertion is only `response.should_not be_success`, it can’t distinguish “missing embed_url” from “host not set”, so the missing-param behavior is not actually tested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:41 — Mocks are unconstrained (`TopicEmbed.expects(:topic_id_for_embed)` and `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` have no `.with(...)`), so passing the wrong embed_url, dropping `user_id`, or dropping `no_throttle` would still pass

app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:9 — New job has no spec at all: the `InvalidParameters` guard, the `User.where(id:).first` lookup, and the `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` mapping are only reached incidentally through a fully mocked controller test

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new job `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb) and there is no corresponding spec file for it in the diff, while other new components do have specs. However, “no spec at all” is a test-coverage/maintainability observation, not a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the code itself. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:56 — absolutize_urls` has no direct spec; uncovered edge cases include protocol-relative `//host/x` URLs, relative paths without a leading slash, and the non-80/443 port branch at line 59 (never exercised)

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` rewrites any `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')`. That condition also matches protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x`, which would be incorrectly rewritten to the source site’s `prefix` (e.g., `http://source.host/cdn.example.com/x`). It also intentionally ignores other relative forms (e.g., `images/x`, `../x`), and the non-80/443 port branch is not exercised by the added spec (which only covers leading-slash relatives on default ports). So the finding’s “uncovered edge cases” are real and at least one (protocol-relative) is a concrete correctness bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:34 — No test for re-importing identical content: the `content_sha1` dedup path (skip revision, no `update_column`) is never exercised, and no test asserts `content_sha1` is actually updated after a changed re-import

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add TopicEmbed.import with a branch where identical content (same content_sha1) skips revision and does not update the embed record. The added spec (spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb) covers creating a new URL and re-importing with changed content, but it does not assert that topic_embeds.content_sha1 changes on update, nor does it exercise the “identical content” no-op branch. However, this is a test-coverage observation, not a verifiable defect in the implementation itself (the code’s behavior for identical content is intentional).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — The new `save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` behavior has no test; the only caller-side test (spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:40) uses content that passes validations anyway, so skip_validations vs. not is indistinguishable

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`. It’s true the added behavior (conditionally skipping validations) isn’t explicitly asserted by any new/changed spec in this diff, and `TopicEmbed` specs don’t differentiate the two paths. However, “no test covers this new behavior” is not itself a concrete defect/bug/security/correctness problem in the code; it’s a test-coverage concern. The code change is also internally consistent with the existing `skip_validations` option used by callers in the diff (e.g., `TopicEmbed.import`/`revise!`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:44 — import_remote` (used by TopicRetriever#fetch_http and lib/tasks/disqus.thor) has zero coverage — no spec stubs `open(url)`/Readability, so the main HTTP import path and `opts[:title]` fallback are untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which performs network I/O via `open(url).read` and parses with `Readability::Document`, with a title fallback `opts[:title] || doc.title`. The added specs cover `TopicEmbed.import` and `TopicRetriever#retrieve` gating behavior, but do not exercise `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` / `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` end-to-end, nor `TopicEmbed.import_remote` directly. There are no tests stubbing `open(url)` or `Readability::Document`, so the primary HTTP import path and the `opts[:title]` override behavior are indeed untested in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:130 — The new `raw_html` cook short-circuit is only covered indirectly via TopicEmbed; there is no post-level test that a `cook_method: regular` post still goes through the analyzer/`Plugin::Filter` pipeline, nor that the migration default leaves existing posts on the regular path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `cook_method` enum and a short-circuit in `Post#cook` for `:raw_html`, plus a migration default and TopicEmbed specs that exercise the raw_html path. It’s true there is no explicit spec asserting the regular/default path still runs through `post_analyzer.cook`/`Plugin::Filter`, but that is a test coverage suggestion rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff. The migration default being correct depends on how `Enum` maps values (not shown here), so the claim that existing posts might not remain on the regular path is speculative and not demonstrably a real problem from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:16 — New embed script (iframe creation and the `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` postMessage origin check) has no JS test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new client-side script (app/assets/javascripts/embed.js) but does not add any corresponding JavaScript tests. However, “no JS test coverage” is a process/coverage observation rather than a concrete bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the code itself, and the diff does not establish a project requirement that all JS changes must include tests.
